Hi Markus,

We are preparing for our SOC 2 readiness review and need to collect evidence around access provisioning and identity controls for Redwood systems used by HealthOps. Can you provide the following artifacts by EOD Friday?

- SCIM provisioning logs for the last 90 days (sample) showing provision/deprovision events and user attributes (redact PII if needed)

- A role matrix describing built-in roles, their permissions, and how RBAC is enforced (CSV preferred)
- Evidence of periodic role review (e.g., a report or screenshot of last review)
- Short explanation of how least-privilege is enforced for service accounts and platform admins

We can accept redacted files or a secure Drive link. Let me know if you need an NDA or DPA in place first.

Thanks,

Markus / team — attaching the first bundle:
- redwood_saml_metadata.xml (SAML SP metadata, includes ACS/assertion consumer URL and cert thumbprint)
- scim_provisioning_sample.log (sanitized sample, shows POSTs to /scim/v2/Users with provisioning events)
- role_matrix_2026Q3.csv (roles, permissions, enforcement points)

Quick answers:
- SCIM: We support SCIM 2.0 for automated provisioning. HealthOps can push users from Okta; attribute mapping includes email, displayName, externalId, groups. Deprovision flows send a "DELETE" or set active=false depending on IdP config.
- SAML: SP metadata attached; assertion includes NameID (email) and groups claim mapping. We support cert rollover and DH key exchange for metadata refresh.
- RBAC & least-privilege: Roles are separated between console, API, and runtime; high-privilege actions require MFA and are logged. Service accounts are scoped with time-limited tokens and least-privilege by default.

I attached a sanitized SCIM provisioning sample (events anonymized) and the role matrix CSV. I also dropped a runbook link with full mapping and internal audit notes: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-scim-runbook

Attachments: redwood_saml_metadata.xml, scim_provisioning_sample.log, role_matrix_2026Q3.csv

Let me know what else the auditor needs — if they want raw logs we should coordinate redaction with Naomi.

— Monica

Thanks for pulling this together. A few legal/contract items before we share raw logs externally:

- HealthOps asked whether an NDA/DPA is needed. If they require more than standard data handling terms, ask them to sign the DocuSign NDA I linked.
- Redaction: do not share raw PII (emails can be redacted if they are not required for the auditor). Share sampled event IDs and timestamps; replace user identifiers with surrogate IDs when possible.
- SOC 2 attestation: we can share a redacted SOC 2 scope PDF; Monica please add the minimal identifying information redwood is comfortable sharing (attachment: soc2_scope_redacted.pdf).

I have no objection to sharing the metadata, role matrix, and the anonymized provisioning sample. For access logs beyond 90 days we need a formal request and a verification of authority.
